about: Battery materials company producing silicon-based anode material (Titan Silicon) to replace graphite in lithium-ion batteries, aiming to raise energy density in electric vehicles and consumer electronics. Customers are battery makers and carmakers such as Panasonic and Mercedes-Benz, and it operates a large plant in Moses Lake, Washington. Headquartered in Alameda, California; founded 2011 by former Tesla and Apple engineers. Venture-backed with a valuation reported above 3 billion dollars. B2B materials supplier with little consumer brand awareness.

Japanese automaker selling Nissan, Infiniti and Datsun vehicles, including the Leaf electric car, Ariya, Qashqai and the GT-R, with Renault and Mitsubishi in a long-standing alliance. Sells cars to consumers and fleets worldwide, producing several million vehicles a year and employing over 100,000 people. Headquartered in Yokohama; founded 1933. Listed in Tokyo (7201). Has been restructuring after sharp losses in 2024 and 2025. Household global brand, active in motorsport as a Formula E manufacturer, Super GT and a long-time FIFA and sports sponsor.

wiki.title: Nissan
wiki.text: Nissan Motor Co., Ltd., known simply as Nissan, trading as the Nissan Motor Corporation, and stylized as NISSAN, is a Japanese multinational automobile manufacturer headquartered in Yokohama, Kanagawa, Japan. The company sells its vehicles under the Nissan and Infiniti brands, and formerly the Datsun brand, with in-house performance tuning products under the Nismo and Autech brands. The company can be traced back to the beginning of the 20th century with the Nissan zaibatsu, or Nissan Group.

about: Alkegen is a specialty materials company making engineered products such as battery and thermal protection materials, filtration media, fiber insulation and silicon anode materials for EV batteries, industrial and aerospace uses. Customers are automakers, industrial, energy and consumer product companies; Crunchbase notes automotive and industrial focus. Headquartered in Irving, Texas, formed from Unifrax and Lydall, backed by private equity firm Altus Capital Partners. B2B, little consumer brand awareness; limited public detail beyond this.

about: Global automotive technology supplier producing vehicle architecture, active safety and ADAS software, connectors, wiring and displays for car makers; it has been separating its electrical distribution systems business. Customers are global automakers, with revenue around 20 billion dollars and over 100,000 employees. Legally domiciled in Schaffhausen, Switzerland; origins in Delphi Automotive with major operations in Troy, Michigan and Dublin. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (APTV). B2B brand with limited public awareness, though Aptiv has sponsored motorsport, notably as a Jaguar TCS Racing partner in Formula E.

wiki.title: Aptiv
wiki.text: Aptiv PLC is a supplier of automotive technology and components. It is organized in Jersey and is a resident of Schaffhausen, Switzerland, for tax purposes. The company operates 139 major manufacturing facilities and 11 major technical centers and has a presence in 50 countries.

about: Automotive Cells Company (ACC) is a European joint venture of Stellantis, Mercedes-Benz and TotalEnergies' Saft, building lithium-ion battery gigafactories to supply electric cars. Its first plant is in Billy-Berclau Douvrin, northern France, with further sites planned in Germany and Italy, some of which were postponed. Customers are the shareholders and other carmakers; the input shows around 4.4 billion euros in funding. Headquartered in Bruges, near Bordeaux. B2B and privately held, so little consumer awareness.

Global manufacturer of plastic components and systems for the automotive industry, including air induction and fluid management parts, interior and exterior trim, and fuel systems. Customers are carmakers worldwide, which it supplies from a network of plants across North America, Europe and Asia. Headquartered in Toronto, Ontario; it was acquired by private equity firm Apollo Global Management in 2021 (previously owned by Cerberus and Tinicum) and is privately held. B2B supplier with essentially no consumer brand awareness.

about: Zhiji Auto, known as IM Motors, is a Shanghai-based premium electric vehicle brand jointly backed by SAIC Motor, Zhangjiang Hi-Tech and Alibaba, selling IM L6, LS6 and LS7 smart EVs, including solid-state battery ambitions. It sells to consumers mainly in China and has started expanding in Europe. Raised about 12 billion yuan in funding. Mid-market consumer awareness in China, growing, supported by Alibaba's technology and SAIC's manufacturing.

about: FAW Pentium (Bestune) is a Chinese passenger car brand under state-owned FAW Group, selling sedans and SUVs such as the T77, T99 and NAT electric models mainly to consumers in China, with some exports. Based in Changchun, Jilin, where FAW is headquartered; Pentium started as a Mazda-based licensed model. Funding listed is about 10.9 billion yuan. Established mid-market domestic brand in China, with limited recognition abroad.

about: IONITY is a European high-power charging network operator for electric vehicles, with over 5,000 charging points at about 800 sites across 25 countries, serving drivers from partners including BMW, Ford, Hyundai Kia, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen and Stellantis, and with a new investment partner BlackRock. Established 2017 as a joint venture of car manufacturers. Headquartered in Munich. Privately held. Recognisable to EV drivers in Europe; its stations are on motorways, not consumer retail, and it has done motorsport marketing.

Erisha E Mobility is an Indian electric vehicle manufacturer based in New Delhi, said by Crunchbase to provide electric vehicles. The input does not provide the product lines, customer segments, scale or ownership, and funding is shown as about 1 billion dollars. Limited public information - check before outreach.

about: First Brands Group is a US automotive aftermarket parts maker whose brands include Fram filters, Autolite spark plugs, Trico wipers, Raybestos brakes, Luk clutches and Carter fuel systems. Sells through retailers such as AutoZone and Advance, and to installers. Headquartered in Rochester Hills, Michigan; owned by Patrick James and private equity. It filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September 2025 amid financing controversies involving off-balance-sheet debt. Consumer-facing brand names are well known to car owners, such as Fram.

XCMG Automobile is the automotive division of XCMG Group, one of the world's largest construction machinery makers, producing heavy trucks, special-purpose vehicles and truck mixers in China. Based in Xuzhou, Jiangsu, and state-linked via the group. Funding listed is about 6.4 billion yuan. B2B commercial vehicle maker with little consumer awareness outside China, though XCMG as a group is a visible name in construction equipment.

about: Textainer Group Holdings is one of the largest lessors of intermodal shipping containers, leasing standard dry containers and refrigerated containers to shipping lines worldwide. Headquartered in San Francisco, California, with an origin in Bermuda. It was acquired by Stonepeak, the private equity infrastructure investor, in a deal announced in 2024 for about 7.4 billion dollars in enterprise value, and delisted from the New York Stock Exchange (TGH). B2B leasing company with no consumer awareness.

Splend is an Australian vehicle subscription and rental service for gig economy drivers, supplying cars to people working for ride-hailing and delivery platforms such as Uber and DoorDash on weekly plans, and has also offered long-term rentals. Headquartered in Sydney. Funding shown is around 800 million dollars including debt facilities. B2B-ish consumer brand known in the gig driving community, with limited broader awareness.

Robo.ai is a mobility and robotics technology company based in Dubai that provides EV, logistics and autonomous mobility services, per Crunchbase. Funding shown is about 580 million dollars. about: Getaround is a Paris-founded car-sharing marketplace, now US-based after a 2022 SPAC merger, letting owners rent out vehicles to drivers through its app with keyless access, in cities in the US and Europe. It earns a share of rental fees and insurance. It was listed on the NYSE (GETR) and exited the US market in early 2025, wound down parts of its business and focuses on Europe. Funding about $763m. A consumer-facing mobility app with modest awareness.

Horse Powertrain is a London-registered powertrain company formed in 2022 as a joint venture between Renault Group and Geely, with Aramco joining as a 10 percent investor in 2024. It builds combustion engines, hybrid systems and transmissions, with plants and R&D in Europe, Brazil, China and Turkey, and about 19,000 employees. Customers include Renault, Dacia, Geely brands and other carmakers. B2B component maker, with the Horse name known in the car industry only.

wiki.title: Horse Powertrain
wiki.text: Horse Powertrain Limited is a joint venture holding aimed at producing powertrains, including internal combustion engines (ICE) and hybrid systems. The venture holding was established in May 2024 and is equally owned by Renault and Geely. It is headquartered in London, United Kingdom.

about: Allison Transmission Holdings is an Indianapolis maker of fully automatic transmissions for medium- and heavy-duty commercial vehicles, buses, fire trucks, defence vehicles and off-highway equipment, along with electrified propulsion systems. It sells to truck and bus makers and the military, with revenue of about $3bn and plants in Indiana and Hungary and India. Listed on the NYSE (ALSN). B2B supplier; the brand is known to fleet operators but not to consumers.

ECD Automotive Design is a Kissimmee, Florida company that restores and customises classic Land Rover Defenders and Range Rovers, and since 2024 other vehicles, as bespoke luxury builds, sometimes with electric conversions, with prices well into six figures. It builds vehicles for wealthy individual clients and shows them on social media and TV. Listed on the NYSE (ECDA) in 2023 via a SPAC merger. Niche premium brand with strong social-media following among car enthusiasts.

Tier IV is a Tokyo autonomous driving software company, founded in 2015, which develops and maintains the open-source Autoware platform and licenses self-driving software for buses, trucks and robotaxis. Investors include Yamaha Motor, Suzuki, Sompo and Sony-affiliated funds, and it works with Japanese cities and mobility operators. Private. B2B technology known in autonomous driving circles, with no consumer awareness.

DeepWay is a Hefei, Anhui-based Chinese company developing intelligent electric heavy-duty trucks and autonomous driving systems for logistics, including electric and hydrogen trucks, as part of Baidu's former and Chinese investor-backed commercial vehicle push. It has raised about $590m, with a January 2026 round. Private, with an IPO plan in Hong Kong. B2B logistics technology brand, known in Chinese trucking, with no consumer awareness.
